clue.text: Fortune put on striking team, one at long odds

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, as if put on the end of it

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a team is a side
fortune here means chance or luck

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a fortune on a team that has gone on strike, a real long shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner with only a slim prospect of winning, priced at long odds, is a long shot.

clue.text: Opposed to taking sides as an alternative

definitions.meaning: hands are sides, so on the opposite side is a cryptic reading
said when introducing a contrasting point, meaning alternatively

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take sides, preferring an alternative view.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a contrasting viewpoint, and literally places something at the opposite side.

clue.text: End a relationship?

definitions.meaning: to finish off or conclude, as with loose ends
a link or association between two parties

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to break off a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means finish or settle; as a noun it means a link or connection.

clue.text: Undecided, where similar ideas may be foolish or clever

definitions.meaning: unable to make up one's mind

definitions.text: where similar ideas may be foolish or clever
definitions.meaning: alludes to the saying that great minds think alike, but fools seldom differ

explanation.surface: An indecisive person muses that shared ideas may be wise or daft.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'great minds think alike' has the retort 'fools seldom differ': the same thought held by a pair of people could be clever or foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being torn between two choices is the idiomatic sense of wavering.

clue.text: Drug causing awkward spell for some

definitions.meaning: a word many people misspell, so spelling it is awkward

explanation.surface: A drug brings on an unpleasant episode for some users.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like a period or a trance; it is spelling, since many writers get the C and S of this word wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The street name for MDMA, a common club drug, also a famously tricky word to spell.

clue.text: Less ostentatious when casting line in river

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line into a river, being less showy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: More modest or unassuming is a comparative synonym for less showy.

clue.text: Cattle lacking water

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or cows

explanation.surface: Herd animals go without water.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for cattle, and the barman's word for spirits served without water or ice.

clue.text: Old record one book contains is to be a perfect example

parts.note: EP, extended play, a vinyl record format of the past
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the big book holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old record that a single book contains is held up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: To typify or embody something is to serve as its ideal instance.

clue.text: Near underground tunnels to be abandoned?

definitions.text: Near underground tunnels to be abandoned?

parts.words: Near underground tunnels to be abandoned?
parts.note: read as approaching the sewers below ground, it means being wasted or lost

explanation.surface: Disused underground tunnels nearby are due to be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: Drains are tunnels under the ground, so to approach them is to head downwards into them; the phrase means to be wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes effort or money being lost entirely, as if flushed away.

clue.text: Time to raise what's heavy crime

parts.note: to heft is to lift something weighty

explanation.surface: It is time to lift a heavy burden, a serious offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a specific criminal offence.

clue.text: Congenial company? I'm in dispute with one leading off

indicators.note: the numeral comes first, ahead of the abbreviation for company
the first two letters sit within the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
taken as the letters I and M
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firm asks if it is friendly while its boss, quarrelling, storms off.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowing from Italian and Spanish meaning pleasant, likeable and like-minded.

clue.text: Blame devious European about trick that may be used

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the trick
something devious takes a winding course, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: A crafty European shifts the blame around through some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges BLAME into MABLE, and 'about' wraps it round PLOY to give MPLOYABLE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable or fit to be put to work can be described as employable.

clue.text: One's playing a leading part

parts.note: a lone performer taking the principal role in a piece of music

explanation.surface: An actor takes the starring role.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece performed by a single musician gives that player the whole lead.

clue.text: Ted appears so stupid!

parts.note: these three letters form the second half of the word meaning possessing wits

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that Ted looks foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is a name in the surface; read it as letters, it is the latter half of WITTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sense, foolish, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: One fellow appearing in irritable state, having sworn

indicators.note: the two letters show up inside the word for irritable

parts.note: testy means irritable or tetchy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man in a tetchy mood has been cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' belongs to the definition, not to 'irritable state': to declare under oath is what a witness does.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving evidence after taking the oath means making a sworn statement.

clue.text: Managed to thwart lexicographer's space-saving device

parts.note: to swing something is to manage or wangle it
to dash hopes is to thwart them

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to frustrate a dictionary-maker's economy measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde-like mark used in dictionaries to stand for the headword, saving space.

clue.text: Apply new dressing

parts.note: dressing in the military sense of lining up troops, done again

explanation.surface: A nurse puts a fresh bandage on a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress ranks by straightening the line, so redressing is putting into line again.
explanation.definitionFit: To put back into a straight line or new arrangement is to redo the alignment.

clue.text: Country road — cue for a detour?

indicators.note: a detour takes a roundabout path, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road sign in the country gives the cue to divert.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation on the equator.

clue.text: Lose control of little animal outside overseas port

indicators.note: the small animal goes around the port

parts.note: a runt is the smallest of a litter
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A small creature escapes its keeper near a foreign harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave wildly and without restraint is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: French involved in sheer disaster needed to perk up!

indicators.note: the letters are wrapped up inside the jumbled word
a disaster leaves things in a mess, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman caught up in a total catastrophe needs cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges SHEER into REESH, and 'involved in' puts FR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive or reinvigorate someone is to liven them up.

clue.text: Put in type of learning process for an award

indicators.note: the verb goes inside the learning method

parts.note: rote is learning by repetition
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A teacher installs a learning method to win a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Great — it's good in colour

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for colour

parts.note: a hue is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a colour is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous or vast is a synonym for great in size.

clue.text: Going without a second helping

parts.note: read not as a diner refused more food but as acting with no aide or assistant

explanation.surface: A diner forgoes another portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' suggests seconds at dinner; it is a boxer's second or helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting alone with no aid is doing something without support.

clue.text: Originally cancelled industrial action in transport system

indicators.note: the original letter, at the start, is struck out

parts.note: a strike is a walkout by workers

explanation.surface: A strike on the transport network was called off at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeled cycle is a simple means of getting about.

clue.text: Wide boy has bigwigs over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: A cocky lad has important people above him.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a flashy small-time crook, the same as a spiv.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a flashy, shady dealer in black-market goods.

clue.text: New analysis of a protein, where vision starts to blur

indicators.note: analysing something breaks it down into its parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh study of a protein reveals where eyesight fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysis of' rearranges A PROTEIN into EARPOINT, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: The optician's term for the closest distance at which the eye can focus clearly.

clue.text: Forest beaten, agitated boy finally left

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
the boy's name departs from the end of the word

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy left at last after being beaten and upset in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally left' removes TED from the end of AGITATED, leaving AGITA, which 'beaten' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest of subarctic Russia and Canada.

clue.text: Maybe take advantage of cutting point made in tease

indicators.note: the second piece is set within the first

parts.note: to have someone on is to tease them
the sharp side of a blade

explanation.surface: A joker sharpens a blade to make fun of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVE ON, to tease, is split around THE EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slightly ahead of a rival, holding an advantage over them.
